title: Thirty robes
translation: Once, when Tokiyori went to pray at the Tsurugaoka shrine, he sent a messenger ahead to Ashikaga Yoshiuji and then dropped in on him. Here is what the host served: dried abalone with the first round of drinks, shrimp with the second, rice cakes with the third, and that was all. At the table were the host and his wife, and Ryūben, the head priest of the shrine, sitting on the hosts' side.
Then Tokiyori said, "About the dyed cloth from Ashikaga that you send me every year. I've been wondering whether it's coming this year."
"It's ready," said Yoshiuji. He had thirty pieces of cloth in all sorts of colours made into robes by the women of the house, right there in front of his guest, and sent them over afterwards.
Someone who saw it all lived until quite recently, and told me about it.

あるじまうけられたりけるやう、{一献|いつこん}に{打鮑|うちあはび}、{二献|にこん}にえび、{三献|さんこん}にかい{餅|もちひ}にて{止|や}みぬ。
その{座|ざ}には、{亭主|ていす}{夫婦|ふうふ}、{隆弁|りゆうべん}{僧正|そうじやう}、あるじ{方|がた}の{人|ひと}にて{坐|ざ}せられけり。

「{用意|ようい}し{候|さうらふ}。」とて、いろいろの{染物|そめもの}{三十|さんじふ}、{前|まへ}にて、{女房|にようばう}どもに{小袖|こそで}に{調|てう}ぜさせて、{後|のち}につかはされけり。

literal: The lay priest of Saimyōji, on the occasion of a visit to the Tsurugaoka shrine, first sent a messenger to the lay priest Ashikaga, Head of the Left Stables, and dropped in, and
the way the host entertained him: with the first round, beaten abalone; with the second round, shrimp; with the third round, kaimochi; and it stopped there.
At that gathering, the master of the house and his wife, and the bishop Ryūben, were seated as people of the host's side.
Then, when (Tokiyori) said, 'I am anxious about the Ashikaga dyed goods that I receive every year',
(the host) said, 'I have them ready', and had thirty dyed pieces of various kinds made into kosode by the women, in front (of the guest), and sent them afterwards.
A person who saw it at that time was alive until recently, and told it (to me).

notes.text: Tsurugaoka Hachimangū, the main shrine of Kamakura and of the shogunate. For Tokiyori, see section 215.

Ashikaga Yoshiuji (1189–1255), son of Yoshikane, as the 1925 edition says. {左馬|さま}: his court post, head of the Left Stables; {入道|にふだう}: he had taken vows. He was an ancestor of the later Ashikaga shoguns. The family's home was Ashikaga in Shimotsuke, today's Tochigi.

{献|こん}: a round of drinks, each with its own small dish. {打鮑|うちあはび}: abalone beaten thin and dried (the 1925 edition's gloss), a standard dish at warrior ceremonies. にて{止|や}みぬ: 'and it stopped there'. Three modest dishes, and nothing more.
Rice cakes or dumplings of some kind. The 1925 edition says it is today's ohagi, rice balls covered in sweet bean paste. Scholars do not agree on the exact dish (compare section 236).
The 1925 edition gives the reading ていす for {亭主|ていす}, 'master of the house' (modern ていしゅ).
Ryūben (1208–1283), head of the Tsurugaoka shrine-temple (the 1925 edition: its {別当|べつたう}). {僧正|そうじやう} is a high rank in the official hierarchy of monks; the translation leaves it out.
{心|こころ}もとなし: 'uneasy, impatient'. The 1925 edition explains: worried whether he will get it this year. The most powerful man in the east, asking politely after his present.
{小袖|こそで}: a robe with small sleeve openings, at the time worn under other clothes, later the basic garment that became the kimono. {調|てう}ぜさせて: 'had them made up' (the 1925 edition: had them sewn).
き again: Kenkō heard it from an eyewitness who died not long before.
